item.title: CPU Support and Power Capping
item.description:
How Joulie caps the CPU packages of a node and sets their frequency governor, through NodeTwin intents the agent enforces.

Contract model

CPU intent is in NodeTwin.spec.cpu. The first field present wins:

  1. packagePowerCapWatts: an absolute cap.
  2. packagePowerCapPctOfMax: a percentage of the node’s cap range.

Policy behavior

Profile CPU cap CPU governor on a CPU-only node, when governor control is on
performance (or draining) high, often 100 % CPU_GOVERNOR_PERFORMANCE_PRESET, default performance
eco lower CPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_PRESET, default efficiency (provisional)

See Governor policy.

item.title: GPU Support (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel)
item.description:
How Joulie caps the GPUs of a node and sets their clock governor on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel, through NodeTwin intents the agent enforces.

Validation status

GPU support has been validated in simulator mode only; the host code paths are written for bare-metal NVIDIA, AMD and Intel nodes, which have not run them yet.

Contract model

NodeTwin.spec.gpu.powerCap holds a per-GPU cap with scope: perGpu. The first field present wins:

  1. capWattsPerGpu: an absolute cap.
  2. capPctOfMax: a percentage of the per-GPU maximum.

The same cap applies to every GPU of the node.

item.title: Hardware Modeling and Physical Power Model
item.description:
This page says what Joulie models about CPUs and GPUs and where the numbers come from. The agent uses these facts to resolve caps; the simulator uses them to turn utilization and controls into power and slowdown.

In the simulator these models are a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: they rest on vendor figures, public measurements and assumptions. What meaningful experiments need is tracked in the milestone Evidence-based evaluation.
